The experience

A premium route that still feels human.

More than a list of places. It's timing, comfort, local context, and the feeling of being looked after by someone who knows Jordan.

Petra at the right hour. Wadi Rum after the crowds.

Days are planned around light, heat, walking time, and the quiet windows most visitors miss.

No rigid group schedule

Stay longer where it matters, skip what isn't worth it, and keep each day realistic instead of rushed.

Local stops you can't Google

Tea with a Bedouin family, a viewpoint off the trail, the bakery locals actually queue for.

Paced around real conditions

Heat, crowds, and road time are built into the plan — so nothing feels like a race.

Sample route

A first Jordan trip that actually flows.

The final plan shifts around your arrival airport, hotel level, travel dates, walking comfort, and must-see places.

Day 1

Amman welcome

Airport pickup, city viewpoints, downtown food, local coffee, and an easy first night.

Day 2

Jerash or Madaba

Roman ruins, mosaics, Mount Nebo, Ajloun hills, or a route shaped by your interests.

Day 3

Petra properly

Early entry, the Siq, the Treasury, viewpoints, an optional Monastery hike, and time to breathe.

Day 4

Wadi Rum overnight

Jeep route, sunset tea, camp dinner, stargazing, and the silence people come to Jordan for.

Day 5

Dead Sea reset

Float, relax, scenic stops, then return to Amman or continue south to Aqaba.
